title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
gist: Keun Lee argues that indiscriminate public investment in poorer regions yields limited economic returns; investment should instead be concentrated in areas that can become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities. Excerpt only.

insights.claim: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities may be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited.
insights.speaker: KEUN LEE
insights.so_what: Spreading fiscal support thinly is a low-return policy; expect better returns where investment is concentrated.

insights.claim: Public investment should be concentrated in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.
insights.speaker: KEUN LEE
insights.so_what: Watch policies favoring second-tier hub cities for regional productivity gains.

insights.claim: Regional inequality takes different forms: capital versus the rest in South Korea and the United Kingdom, north versus south in Italy, and coastal versus inland in China and the United States.
insights.speaker: KEUN LEE
insights.so_what: Regional divides are a widespread political and economic fault line across major economies.
